parallel.requirements: The parent recognized exact CLI parity, ESM .mjs structure, local-only imports, pure JavaScript JWT/JWS behavior, Python repr/JSON formatting, and no external modules.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: It split the implementation into child-owned hashing, JSON/repr, argparse, and JOSE modules, then added separate compliance and adversarial fuzzing verifier children while the parent wrote the entry file and harnesses.
parallel.implementation: The final artifact contained test10.mjs plus codec, hash, py, and jose modules; child agents wrote most library modules and the parent made surgical JOSE fixes after testing.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Integration happened through the shared /output tree and parent-level harness runs; artifact validation found test10.mjs and the module tree present.
parallel.verification: The parent ran a 94-case differential harness and consumed a clean compliance audit, but the adversarial fuzz child found divergences and did not return a completed report before timeout.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The process timed out with an empty final response and with the fuzz verifier interrupted after concrete findings; official evaluation still failed at 31/70.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same prompt constraints, including exact argparse behavior, byte-exact JWT output, ESM modules, and no external dependencies.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One parent trajectory owned probing, implementation, integration, testing, cleanup, and final verification without any subagent or delegation activity.
serial.implementation: It wrote codec, hash, JSON/repr, argparse, JOSE, and entry modules and repeatedly edited argparse and JWS details after differential failures.
serial.integration_and_delivery: All files were created directly in /output and validated by local syntax checks, sample runs, and final suite reruns before the process timed out.
serial.verification: It ran four sample cases, a 35-case harness, short-option tests, a 155-case fuzz script, and final regression reruns that reported zero local failures.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Despite local checks passing, the official evaluator completed at 31/70 and solution_passed false; the trajectory does not expose a single proven hidden-test cause.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the full Python-to-ESM port requirements and probed JWT, repr, argparse, Unicode, and option edge cases.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same requirements from the identical prompt and also probed sample output, CLI errors, Unicode, and option behavior.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-recognition gap explains the equal official failure; both targeted exact output and no external dependencies.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel assigned major components to children, including hashing, JSON/repr, argparse, JOSE, compliance, and fuzz verification.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all component implementation, fixes, tests, and cleanup in the single parent trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel created inter-agent result lifecycle risk; serial avoided delegation but spent the entire budget in one long local implementation loop.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs generally gave concrete file paths, exports, and verification obligations for separately owned modules.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no cross-agent handoff boundary and maintained module contracts inside the same working context.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The material context difference was not missing interface detail; it was the late verifier result that never returned to the parent.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel assembled a larger module tree with separate codec, hash, py, and jose layers, much of it produced by children and then tested by the parent.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial built a similar but smaller module tree directly, then made targeted fixes to argparse and JWS behavior in sequence.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both implementations reached locally passing harnesses, but parallel's later child-discovered divergences were not folded back before closure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel received several child results but the randomized fuzz verifier was killed while the parent was waiting and before its findings returned as a final result.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial's checks were direct local commands, so their pass/fail results returned immediately to the same owner.
comparison_dimensions.difference: This is the main process difference: parallel lost a verifier finding at a child-parent boundary, while serial directly observed its regression outputs.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel integrated through a shared /output directory; child modules and parent edits coexisted, and the compliance child made a narrow final comment fix.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial integrated all writes locally and performed cleanup after finding forbidden-token strings in its own generated tree.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No concrete write collision or overwrite caused the official score gap because there was no score gap; shared state was observable but not the retained failure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel accepted a 94/94 fixed harness and clean compliance audit, but the deeper fuzzing child had found divergences before being interrupted.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed its 35-case, 19-case, 155-case, and final regression checks directly in the parent trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a stricter delegated verifier in flight whose findings did not return; serial had less child lifecycle risk but still did not pass official hidden evaluation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used the full 2399-second process budget, returned code 143, and had an empty final response after waiting for the fuzz child.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also used the full 2399-second process budget and timed out after its final local regression command returned.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both closed by timeout, but parallel's timeout trapped a live child verifier result, whereas serial's final command result had already reached the parent.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed status.json evaluations make this a both_fail pair: both artifacts passed 31 of 70 official samples and solution_passed is false. The concrete task-solving difference is procedural, not an official pass/fail split: the parallel run delegated verification and lost a child-discovered fuzz finding at timeout, while the serial run observed its local final regression outputs directly before its own timeout. The evidence does not support a unique hidden-test root cause for either artifact.
parallel_contributors: Delegated adversarial fuzzing found invalid UTF-8 and Unicode printability divergences but did not return a completed report or fixes before timeout.
The parent spent closure time waiting for the fuzzer after a 94/94 fixed harness and a clean compliance result.
serial_contributors: The serial parent iteratively fixed argparse behavior and directly observed final local regression outputs before timeout.
The serial artifact nevertheless failed the same official evaluation count, so its local checks were not sufficient for hidden acceptance.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The two runs used different module layouts and different local test suites.
The hidden official failure cause is not uniquely established by the trajectory evidence because both completed at the same 31/70 score.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: parallel adverse process pattern, not an outcome-differential root cause
